audience: Passenger-car drivers need to recognize required equipment, visibility limits and occupant-restraint rules before driving.
accuracy: Stopping distances keep the source’s speed and dry-road conditions. Child-seat law and safety recommendations are labeled separately. National crash statistics and weather-adjusted studded-tire dates are isolated as debt.
dynamic: ITD may adjust the seasonal studded-tire dates for weather; check the current official notice before choosing a travel date. National injury and belt-effectiveness statistics need dated primary evidence before use as current figures.
marketAngle: equipment checks, visibility and child restraint decisions
mis: Parking lights do not replace headlights when driving conditions require lights; a child-seat recommendation is distinct from the statutory age requirement.
mnemonic: See, stop and secure is a teaching reminder for visibility, braking and occupant restraints.
glossary: High and low beams light different distances; a parking brake holds the stopped car; an overhanging load extends beyond the vehicle.
skills: Apply child and adult restraint rules
debts: Physical pages forty and forty-two give national child-crash and restraint-effectiveness figures without a dated study in the excerpt; verify dated primary sources before displaying them as current statistics.
The default studded-tire season on physical page forty-two can be changed by ITD for weather; current exceptions are not established.
Antique vehicles and street rods may have different equipment requirements; no detailed exception is supplied on physical page forty-three.
C: Operating another person’s vehicle without consent while intending only to deprive the owner temporarily, rather than steal it, is a misdemeanor.
A mechanically unsafe vehicle must not be driven in Idaho.
The driver is responsible for correcting dangerous defects, missing essential equipment or necessary vehicle repairs.
Idaho does not require a yearly vehicle safety inspection.
An officer who stops a vehicle and finds unsafe conditions or missing required equipment may issue a citation.
A vehicle must have two independent brake systems so one remains usable if the other fails.
On dry pavement, the foot brake must stop a vehicle traveling twenty miles an hour within twenty-five feet.
At twenty miles an hour on dry pavement, the emergency or parking brake must stop the vehicle within fifty-five feet.
The parking brake must keep a parked vehicle from moving on a hill.
A vehicle needs two headlamps providing both high and low beams.
Headlamps must illuminate the road without dazzling approaching drivers.
High beams must make people and vehicles visible at least three hundred fifty feet ahead.
Low beams must illuminate at least one hundred feet of roadway ahead.
Headlights must not be covered with material that is reflective, opaque or non-transparent.
A motor vehicle’s working brake lights must be red or amber and visible at least one hundred feet behind in normal sunlight.
Brake lights must illuminate when the foot brake is applied.
Brake-light lenses should be kept clean.
A vehicle built before January first, nineteen fifty-six needs at least one red rear light.
Except for vehicles built before January first, nineteen fifty-six, a passenger motor vehicle needs two red rear lights, one on each side, visible from five hundred feet behind.
A motor vehicle built after January first, nineteen fifty-five needs driver-controlled flashing electric signals for both left and right turns at front and rear, visible from one hundred feet.
Front electric turn signals must show white or amber light.
Rear electric turn signals must show red or amber light.
Each tire should retain at least two thirty-seconds of an inch of tread.
A motor vehicle must have a horn audible from at least two hundred feet.
A horn producing an unreasonably loud or harsh sound is prohibited.
Vehicle windows and windshields must use approved safety glass.
Damaged window or windshield glass must be replaced when it obstructs the driver’s view.
Windows and windshields must remain free of signs and stickers other than those required by law.
Objects placed or hung inside the vehicle must not block the windows or windshield.
Frost, snow, dirt and other visibility obstructions must be removed from vehicle glass.
Window and windshield treatments must not create a mirrored surface or otherwise make the glass difficult to see through, even from outside.
Every motor vehicle needs windshield wipers that remove rain, snow and other moisture.
A motor vehicle’s rear-view mirror must provide a highway view extending at least two hundred feet behind.
When a load or trailer blocks the usual view through the rear window, the vehicle needs an additional mirror on each side.
A vehicle without a rear-view mirror needs both a left and a right side mirror.
A motor vehicle must have a working muffler that prevents unusual or loud noise.
Motor vehicles and trailers need fenders, wheel covers or flaps that prevent wheel-thrown material from reaching other vehicles.
Trailers and semitrailers need two red rear lights, one on each side, visible from five hundred feet behind.
C2: Children aged six or younger traveling in a non-commercial vehicle must use approved child safety seats under the law applicable to cars built with safety belts after January first, nineteen sixty-six.
A child safety seat must meet federal safety standards.
The child must fit snugly within the safety seat’s own straps.
The child safety seat must be secured to the vehicle.
The child safety seat must be used on every trip.
The handbook recommends reading both the child-seat instructions and the vehicle manual for height and weight limits and correct installation.
The handbook recommends the rear seat for every child younger than thirteen.
The handbook’s safety recommendations say never to place a rear-facing child seat in front of an active passenger airbag.
Idaho requires occupants to wear the safety belts or shoulder restraints supplied as factory equipment in the vehicle.
Safety belts help the driver keep control on winding or rough roads and during collision-avoidance maneuvers.
Red and blue emergency lights are permitted only on emergency vehicles.
Sirens, bells and whistles are listed as prohibited equipment for ordinary vehicles.
A muffler cutout or bypass that increases exhaust noise is prohibited.
A vehicle must not have more than two spotlights.
A vehicle must not have more than two front auxiliary lights.
A vehicle must not have more than two front fog lights.
A vehicle must not have more than two cowl or fender lights.
Headlamps and taillamps must be on between sunset and sunrise.
Poor visibility also requires headlamps and taillamps when needed for safety.
A driver must dim headlights five hundred feet before meeting another vehicle.
A driver must dim headlights two hundred feet before overtaking another vehicle.
When driving requires lights, the driver must use headlights rather than parking lights.
Before driving, the driver must clear ice, snow and dirt from the windows to preserve visibility in every direction.
Passengers and cargo must not block the driver’s view or interfere with vehicle operation.
A load extending at least four feet behind the vehicle needs a red flag at its far end.
The flag on a load projecting at least four feet behind must be at least eighteen inches square.
At night, a load projecting at least four feet behind needs a red light visible from at least five hundred feet in place of the flag.
A vehicle’s load must not project beyond the left fenders.
A vehicle’s load may extend no more than six inches beyond the right fenders.
Reckless driving with willful disregard for people or property is prohibited on both public roads and private property.
A driver must give full attention to operating the vehicle safely.
Failure to attend to safe vehicle operation can result in an inattentive-driving citation.
